guide.storagenexus.start.welcome:
Welcome
Nexium adds drawers and barrels, a storage network, conduits, all-in-one tools, Nexium gear and the Essentials.

Pick a topic on the left, or search for one. Most topics end with the recipes for their items.
guide.storagenexus.start.codex:
Using the Codex
Pick a topic on the left. Click a category to open or close it.

Coloured, underlined words are links: click one to jump there. The < and > buttons go back and forward, and Home comes back here.

Type in the search box to find any topic.

In any inventory, hover over an item and press H to open its page. In a recipe, click an ingredient to open its page.
guide.storagenexus.start.new:
What's new
1.15.0
The Construction Builder builds out from the block you click, with modes, a size, Undo and a Nexus Link.

Right-click a grown crop to harvest and replant it; hold V for the whole field.

The Nexium Ingot is made from a diamond, an emerald, a netherite ingot and a netherite upgrade template.

1.14.5
Drawers are cheaper: planks and slabs, no chest.

1.14.4
The anvil is never Too Expensive: any job can be done for its full cost in levels.

1.14.3
The terminal search follows JEI's and REI's, and their + button shows exactly which ingredients are missing.

1.14.2
Connector priority always comes first: items go to the highest priority inventory that takes them.

The Drawer Controller's reach outline now needs sneak + right-click; a plain right-click shows the drawer count.

1.14.1
The AIOT readout by the hotbar shows for 20 seconds when you switch to an AIOT or press X, Z or V.

1.14.0
The Farm Assembler makes the one-block farms and the Master Librarian: pick one, put in what it needs, press Build. No more renaming chests.

1.13.1
The AIOTs are redrawn at 32x32 in their original colours, and the Fortune and Silk Touch colours show on the gem.

1.13.0
The guide is now the Nexium Codex: one long page per topic, links, search, and H to look up any item.

Every texture is redrawn at 64x64, with new AIOTs and new Nexium armor.

The Dimensional Anchor always loads its 3x3 chunks, and right-clicking it shows them for a minute.

1.12
Five more one-block farms, the Freezer, soul sand to sand in a blast furnace, and Vein Mining without a module.
guide.storagenexus.start.finding:
Finding things
Every item's tooltip says what it does. All items are in the Nexium creative tab.

Press L for advancements: the Nexium tab is a map of the whole mod.

Lost your guide? Craft a book with any drawer.
guide.storagenexus.start.keys:
Key binds
G: tool menu, when holding an AIOT or Nexium tool. With neither: the armor menu.
V: hold to vein mine.
M: Magnet on or off.

Change them in Options > Controls > Key Binds, under Nexium.
guide.storagenexus.start.settings:
Settings
Many features can be tuned or switched off in the config file, nexusessentials.json. Restart to apply changes.

On a server, the server's file counts.

Install Nexium on the server and on every player's game.
guide.storagenexus.drawers.drawers:
Drawers
A drawer stores one kind of item in huge amounts.

1x1: 54 stacks.
1x2: 2 slots of 27.
2x2: 4 slots of 13.5.

All 13 woods, made from that wood's planks and slabs (no chest). Capacity upgrades multiply these.
guide.storagenexus.drawers.using:
Using a drawer
Right-click the front: insert what you hold.
Double-click: insert all matching items from your inventory.
Left-click the front: take a stack.
Sneak + left-click: take one.

Break a drawer by hitting any side but the front.
guide.storagenexus.drawers.bar:
Fullness bar
A bar under each count shows how full it is, upgrades counted:
green: under 75%
yellow: to 90%
red: 90% and up

No bar when empty, unless locked. Fluid and compacting drawers have one too.
guide.storagenexus.drawers.upgrades:
Upgrades
Right-click a drawer with an upgrade to install it.
To see or remove them: right-click a side or the top empty-handed (or sneak + right-click).

Four slots take capacity and Void upgrades; a fifth takes only Lock.
guide.storagenexus.drawers.capacity:
Capacity upgrades
Iron x2
Gold x4
Diamond x8
Emerald x16
Netherite x32

They add together: Iron + Gold = x6. No upgrades = x1.
Not removable if the contents would no longer fit.
guide.storagenexus.drawers.swap:
Swapping upgrades
All four slots full? A better capacity upgrade swaps out the weakest.

Right-click the drawer with it: the old one drops.

Or put it in a slot (shift-click, or click it on): the old one goes to your inventory.
guide.storagenexus.drawers.lockvoid:
Lock and Void
Lock Upgrade: keeps each slot reserved for its item, even when empty. Own slot; padlock top-right on the front.

Void Upgrade: deletes what doesn't fit (handy for cobble farms). Marker top-left. Overflow is destroyed for good!
guide.storagenexus.drawers.fluid:
Fluid Drawer
Holds 32 buckets of one fluid.

Use a bucket on the front to fill or empty it.

Capacity, Lock and Void upgrades work too. A Fluid Intake next to it fills it.
guide.storagenexus.drawers.compacting:
Compacting Drawer
Stores nuggets, ingots and blocks as one pool (any 9-to-1 or 4-to-1 recipe that works both ways).

54 stacks of the largest form, e.g. iron blocks.

Top slot: largest form. Bottom: smaller forms.
guide.storagenexus.drawers.moving:
Moving storage
Breaking a drawer, compacting drawer or fluid drawer keeps everything inside, upgrades included, in the dropped item, like a shulker box.

Hover over the item to see what is inside. Place it anywhere to get it all back.
guide.storagenexus.drawers.controller:
Drawer Controller
Drawers touching it, or each other, within 12 blocks join it.

Right-click with an item: it goes to the drawer holding it.
Double-click: your whole inventory.
Empty hand: shows its drawer count.
Sneak + empty hand: shows its reach for 1 minute (again to hide).
guide.storagenexus.drawers.slave:
Controller Slave
Extends a controller. Place it touching the drawers, or the controller, within 12 blocks of the controller; drawers within 12 blocks of the slave join too.

Slaves chain: a slave within reach of another slave works as well.
guide.storagenexus.drawers.barrels:
Barrels
Five tiers of barrel:
Iron: 45 slots
Gold: 66 slots
Diamond: 84 slots
Emerald: 102 slots
Netherite: 120 slots

Iron has 5 rows of 9, the rest 6 rows of 11, 14, 17 and 20. Bigger ones get a wider screen.
guide.storagenexus.drawers.barrelup:
Barrel upgrades
Right-click a barrel with a Barrel Upgrade to raise its tier in place. What is inside stays inside.

Iron: a vanilla barrel
Gold: an Iron Barrel
Diamond: a Gold Barrel
Emerald: a Diamond Barrel
Netherite: an Emerald Barrel
guide.storagenexus.network.network:
Storage network
A storage network joins many inventories into one big storage, opened from a Crafting Terminal.

No power needed. One network holds up to 2048 cables, connectors and terminals.
guide.storagenexus.network.connector:
Storage Connector
Joins every inventory touching it to the network: chests, barrels, drawers, anything with slots.

Right-click it to set its priority. Items go into the higher priority first, even if a lower one already holds some, and come out of the lower first. At the same priority, items join their own kind.

A Drawer Controller only fills drawers that already hold the item or are locked to it.
guide.storagenexus.network.filtered:
Filtered Connector
Joins only the one inventory it faces, through a filter.

Right-click it to set its priority and put a filter in its slot. It accepts only what the filter lets through.

Craft it from a Storage Connector and a comparator.
guide.storagenexus.network.cable:
Inventory Cable
Joins network blocks into one network. It links Storage and Filtered Connectors, Crafting Terminals, other cables, Fluid Intakes and Dimensional Outputs.

Cables and connectors grow an arm towards each block they link to.
guide.storagenexus.network.terminal:
Crafting Terminal
Shows everything in the network, fluids first, beside a crafting grid.

Left-click: take a stack.
Right-click: take one.
Shift-click: to your inventory.
Holding items: left-click puts all in, right-click puts one in.
guide.storagenexus.network.search:
Search and sort
Type to search by name. Start with @ to search by mod: @minecraft shows only vanilla items.

An arrow button flips the direction; another cycles the sort: # count, A name, @ mod.

Hover an item for its count.
guide.storagenexus.network.extras:
Terminal extras
Bucket on a fluid fills it. A full bucket: left-click pours it in, right-click stores it.

Red X: empties the grid into the network, else your inventory, else the floor.

Bars by the result slot show how full the network is.
guide.storagenexus.network.crafting:
Crafting from it
The recipe book shows what you can make from the network's items. Click a recipe to fill the grid from the network, then your inventory.

JEI and REI: their + button does the same. When something is missing, JEI marks those slots red and REI lists them. Their search box and the terminal's stay the same. Neither mod is needed.
guide.storagenexus.network.bus:
Import/Export Bus
Place it on an inventory or tank, next to a cable.

Import: pulls items and fluids in.
Export: pushes them out.

Right-click: mode and an optional filter. 32 items or a bucket every half second.
guide.storagenexus.network.emitter:
Level Emitter
Connect it to the network. It gives a redstone signal while the network holds at least (or fewer than) an amount of one item.

Right-click it: click the slot with an item, set the amount, choose at least or fewer than. A bucket counts that fluid, in buckets.
guide.storagenexus.network.tablets:
Tablets
Sneak + right-click a Crafting Terminal with a Crafting Storage Tablet to link it.

Right-click the tablet anywhere, in any dimension, to open that network while the terminal's chunk is loaded (an Anchor can keep it so).
guide.storagenexus.network.anchor:
Dimensional Anchor
Keeps the 3x3 chunks around it loaded, all the time: the chunk it stands in and the 8 around it.

When you place it, and whenever you right-click it, it outlines those chunks for 1 minute: the chunk borders as a grid at its height, with posts at the four outer corners. Right-click again to hide the outline.

Removing it lets the chunks unload. Chunks forced by /forceload or other mods stay loaded.
guide.storagenexus.links.links:
Dimensional links
Send items and fluids anywhere: any distance, any dimension.

Click a Dimensional Input with a Dimensional Link Card, then click any Outputs.

What you put in the Input arrives at the Outputs.
guide.storagenexus.links.names:
Link names
Each link has a random name. To choose one, rename the card in an anvil first, or rename it later in either block's screen.

Look at an Input or Output to see its name for 3 seconds.
guide.storagenexus.links.moving:
Moving an Input
Break it, then click the new one with the same card. It takes over the link and all its Outputs.
guide.storagenexus.links.input:
Dimensional Input
Takes items and fluids: by hand, or from hoppers, pipes, conduits and Fluid Intakes.

If nothing can take an item, its buffer backs up.
guide.storagenexus.links.dspeed:
Transfer Speed
The Transfer Speed Upgrade goes in a Dimensional Input's speed slot.

One: 16 items at a time.
Two: full stacks.
guide.storagenexus.links.output:
Dimensional Output
Pushes what arrives into everything around it, on the sides you turn on: inventories, fluid storage, storage network blocks and item conduits (which carry items on to their Insert sides of the same colour).

Inputs are skipped.
guide.storagenexus.links.sides:
Output sides
In an Output's screen, the D, U, N, S, W and E buttons switch sides on and off (green is on). Hover one to see what is on that side.

An Output can hold a filter, so one Input can split items by type.
guide.storagenexus.links.conduits:
Conduits
Item and Fluid conduits, Tier 1 and 2, share one block.

Items: 4 every half second (Tier 2: 16).
Fluids: 100 mB a tick (Tier 2: 2000).

Tier 2 has a green trim; use one on a Tier 1 conduit to upgrade it.
guide.storagenexus.links.wrench:
Conduit Wrench
Right-click a conduit side: cycle its mode (off, insert, extract, both).

Sneak + right-click: all its settings.

Right-click a conduit with a full block to give it a facade. The wrench takes it off.
guide.storagenexus.links.channels:
Colour channels
Each side has an In (insert) and an Out (extract) colour.

What a side extracts goes to sides inserting on the same colour. A Both side can use different colours in and out.

Arm rings: inner = In, outer = Out.
guide.storagenexus.links.settings:
Side settings
Sneak + wrench opens a side's settings: mode, In and Out colours, redstone control, priority, round-robin, filter and speed upgrades. It names what is on that side.

Conduit Speed Upgrade: faster. Up to 3 fit in the speed slot.
guide.storagenexus.links.filters:
Filters
Basic Filter: right-click to set up to 9 items to allow or block.
Advanced Filter: matches by item tag, e.g. every ore.
Fluids: use their bucket.

Filters go in a conduit side, Output, Filtered Connector or Bus.
guide.storagenexus.links.intake:
Fluid Intake
Takes fluid from the source blocks touching it, about a bucket a second, and passes it to a Fluid Drawer, conduit or network next to it. Infinite water is never drained.

Bucket on it: take only that fluid. Sneak + empty hand: any again.
guide.storagenexus.links.lava:
Lava Source
The Infinite Lava Source: put it next to a Fluid Intake for endless lava. It never runs dry.

Craft it from obsidian, lava buckets and a nether star.
guide.storagenexus.links.limits:
Reach and limits
Dimensional links: any distance, any dimension.

Fluid Intake: the blocks touching it.

One conduit line: up to 1024 conduits.
guide.storagenexus.aiot.aiot:
All-in-one tools
A pickaxe, axe, shovel, hoe and sword in one item, in Stone, Copper, Iron, Golden, Diamond, Netherite and Nexium.

It mines what its material's tools mine, as fast as the best of them. An iron AIOT can't mine obsidian; a diamond one can.
guide.storagenexus.aiot.crafting:
Crafting one
Put all five tools of one material (pickaxe, axe, shovel, hoe, sword) anywhere in the crafting grid.

Five fresh tools make a full AIOT, worn ones a worn one. The anvil repair cost of the most expensive tool carries over.
guide.storagenexus.aiot.stats:
Stats
Durability, 1.5 times that of the five tools:
Stone 983
Copper 1,425
Iron 1,875
Golden 240
Diamond 11,708
Netherite 15,233
Nexium 18,750

Attack damage: 9, 9, 9, 7, 9, 10 and 11.
guide.storagenexus.aiot.fighting:
Fighting
Hits as hard as that material's axe, at a sword's speed (1.6 attacks a second). It sweeps like a sword and disables shields like an axe.

It loses 1 durability per hit and per block mined.
guide.storagenexus.aiot.using:
Using an AIOT
Right-click: strips logs, scrapes or unwaxes copper, makes paths (or tills a path into farmland), puts out a lit campfire.

Sneak + right-click: tills grass and dirt.

Every tool and sword enchantment works.
guide.storagenexus.aiot.enchants:
Enchantments
Crafting keeps every enchantment, at the highest level any tool had it.

Sharpness, Smite, Bane of Arthropods: the highest stays (Sharpness wins a tie).

Curses stay too.
guide.storagenexus.aiot.silk:
Silk and Fortune
Both stay: Fortune is active, Silk Touch inactive (the tooltip says so). Switch in the tool menu.

At an anvil, an AIOT with one takes the other from a book or AIOT, added inactive. A grindstone removes the inactive one too.
guide.storagenexus.aiot.upgrade:
Netherite AIOT
At a smithing table: a Diamond AIOT, a netherite upgrade template and a netherite block.

Enchantments (the inactive one too) and wear stay.
guide.storagenexus.aiot.upgrade2:
Nexium AIOT
At a smithing table: a Netherite AIOT, a netherite upgrade template and a Block of Nexium.

Or craft one from five Nexium tools.
guide.storagenexus.aiot.menu:
Tool menu
Hold an AIOT or Nexium tool and press G; press it again or Esc to close.

Mining: switches Silk Touch and Fortune. The gem shows which: green Fortune, blue Silk Touch.

Haste II: Nexium tools only.
guide.storagenexus.aiot.menu2:
Tool menu, more
Modules (AIOTs only): two slots. Put a module in like any item; the button beside it switches it on or off.

Vein size: click to step 4, 9, 18, 32 ... up to the server's limit, then back to 4.

Armor: opens the armor menu.
guide.storagenexus.aiot.modules:
AIOT modules
Two modules, one of each per AIOT. They keep their on/off setting when taken out.

Nexus Link: drops go to a storage network.
3x3 Mining: mines a 3x3 around each block.

Vein mining needs no module.
guide.storagenexus.aiot.nexuslink:
Nexus Link
Sneak + right-click a Crafting Terminal with the module (or an AIOT that has one) to link it.

Drops, Fortune and Silk Touch included, go into that terminal's network in any dimension. Experience still drops.
guide.storagenexus.aiot.nexuslink2:
Nexus Link, more
The terminal's chunk must be loaded: put a Dimensional Anchor near it.

What the network can't take drops as usual.
guide.storagenexus.aiot.area:
3x3 Mining
Mines the 3x3 around the block, facing you: a wall ahead, the floor or ceiling looking down or up.

Only blocks the AIOT is made for, about twice as hard as yours at most, never ones with contents.

X turns it on or off.
guide.storagenexus.aiot.tunnel:
Tunnels
Tunnel (tool menu, or Z) sets how deep a 3x3 digs, away from you: off, 2, 4, 8, 16, 24 or 32 layers.

A faint green outline shows what your next block will take: a vein, a 3x3 or a tunnel. Sneak mines one block.
guide.storagenexus.aiot.vein:
Vein Mining
Mines every touching block of your kind, anything but stone: ores, logs, leaves, hay, melons, obsidian.

Hold V while mining with the right tool. No module needed: the tool menu sets how many blocks (limit 256).
guide.storagenexus.builder.builder:
Construction Builder
Right-click a block to build out from it: every connected block of that kind gets a new one on the face you clicked.

It places the block in your offhand, or else the one you clicked, facing the same way. A pale blue outline shows where they will go.
guide.storagenexus.builder.modes:
Modes and tiers
Extend: the whole connected face. Line: one row, the way you look. Exchange: swaps the face for your offhand block and gives you the old ones.

One click places up to 9 (Iron), 27 (Diamond), 64 (Netherite) or 128 (Nexium, unbreakable). Each block costs 1 durability.
guide.storagenexus.builder.menu:
Builder menu
Press G holding the builder for its menu: mode, plane (any, flat or upright) and size.

Undo takes back your last build and returns its blocks. It remembers 2 builds, until you log out.
guide.storagenexus.builder.link:
Blocks from a network
Put a Nexus Link Module in the builder's menu, then sneak + right-click a Crafting Terminal with the builder to link it.

When your inventory runs out of a block, it takes more from that network. Creative players need no blocks.
guide.storagenexus.builder.crafting:
Crafting one
Iron: paper, lapis and a gold nugget over an iron frame.

Add a diamond to make it Diamond. Its settings and module stay.
guide.storagenexus.builder.upgrade:
Upgrading
At a smithing table with a Netherite Upgrade: Diamond + netherite ingot makes Netherite, and Netherite + Nexium ingot makes Nexium.
guide.storagenexus.aiot.readout:
Outline and readout
Blocks the next swing would also take glow pale green.

A panel by the hotbar shows Silk Touch or Fortune and each module's state for 20 seconds after you switch to an AIOT or press X, Z or V, and while V is held.

Change the time or turn it off in client settings.
guide.storagenexus.aiot.both:
Mining rules
With 3x3 also on, anything but stone is vein mined (key held); stone is 3x3 mined.

Fortune, Silk Touch and Nexus Link apply; each block costs 1 durability.

Sneak: one block only.
A broken AIOT drops its modules.
guide.storagenexus.nexium.nexium:
Nexium
The tier above netherite: tools, armor and a block, all from Nexium ingots. Everything Nexium survives fire and lava.

Nexium armor and its set bonuses are in this category too; the Nexium AIOT is under All-in-one Tools.
guide.storagenexus.nexium.ingot:
Nexium Ingot
A diamond, an emerald, a netherite ingot and a netherite upgrade smithing template, in a crafting table, make 3 ingots. The template is used up.
guide.storagenexus.nexium.block:
Block of Nexium
Nine ingots make a block, and a block makes nine ingots again.

It is a beacon base, mined like a netherite block. Beacons take the ingots as payment.

At a smithing table it turns a Netherite AIOT into a Nexium AIOT.
guide.storagenexus.nexium.gear:
Nexium gear
At a smithing table: a netherite upgrade template, the netherite piece and a Nexium ingot. Enchantments and wear stay.

There is a Nexium sword, pickaxe, axe, shovel, hoe, spear, helmet, chestplate, leggings and boots.
guide.storagenexus.nexium.tools:
Nexium tools
Netherite's mining speed and level, 2,500 uses (netherite 2,031) and enchantability 18.

One more attack damage than netherite: sword 9, axe 11, spear 6.
guide.storagenexus.nexium.spear:
Nexium Spear
Charges and attacks like a vanilla spear, one step past netherite on each spear stat.

It is a netherite spear plus a Nexium ingot at a smithing table.
guide.storagenexus.nexium.haste:
Haste II
The Nexium pickaxe, axe, shovel, hoe and AIOT give the real Haste II effect while held in the main hand.

With Efficiency V they mine as fast as netherite with Efficiency V under a Haste II beacon: stone and netherrack break instantly.
guide.storagenexus.nexium.haste2:
More on Haste II
Like the beacon's, it also speeds up attacks by 20%.

It shows a steady infinity icon and goes when the tool is put away.
guide.storagenexus.nexium.haste3:
Haste, beacons
It doesn't stack with a beacon's Haste II. A beacon's or command's Haste is never taken off.

Switch it off in the tool menu (G).
guide.storagenexus.armor.armor:
Nexium armor
Helmet, chestplate, leggings and boots.

Armor: 4 / 9 / 7 / 4 points, 24 in all (netherite 20).
Toughness: 5 each, 20 in all: the game's maximum.
Knockback resistance: 0.15 each.
Durability: 484 / 704 / 660 / 572.
guide.storagenexus.armor.extras:
Also
It takes armor trims, shown on the item icons too. Baby zombies and the like wear it properly.

Like netherite, it keeps piglins calm. It survives fire and lava.
guide.storagenexus.armor.bonuses:
Set bonuses
Nether-forged (full set): Fire Resistance.

Miner's set (full set): full-speed mining underwater and in the air.

No knockback (full set): hits and explosions don't push you back.
guide.storagenexus.armor.bonuses2:
More bonuses
Nexus restock (full set, linked chestplate): hotbar stacks top up from a storage network, and you eat from it when hungry.

Night vision (helmet): Night Vision.
guide.storagenexus.armor.menu:
Armor menu
Press G with no AIOT or Nexium tool in hand, or click Armor in the tool menu. Each bonus has an on/off switch; bonuses the worn pieces don't give are greyed out.

A setting is saved on the piece that carries it, so it moves with the armor.
guide.storagenexus.armor.effects:
Effects
Fire Resistance and Night Vision are infinite while worn, with a steady icon. They go as soon as a piece comes off or the bonus is switched off.

A potion's or beacon's effect is never taken away.
guide.storagenexus.armor.restock:
Nexus restock
Link the chestplate: sneak + right-click a Crafting Terminal with it.

A hotbar stack you use is topped up from the network at 8 left, or refilled when you use the last one. A stack you move or throw away whole is left alone.
guide.storagenexus.armor.restock2:
Eating from it
When your hunger bar is down by 6 or more, you eat the most filling plain food in the network, never food with effects (golden apples, rotten flesh, pufferfish). Bowls and bottles go back in.

The network is reached as for the Nexus Link module.
guide.storagenexus.essentials.explosions:
Explosions
Creeper and ghast explosions break no blocks, and ghast fireballs light no fires. They still hurt and push players and mobs.

They also spare item frames, paintings, armor stands, dropped items, minecarts and boats.
guide.storagenexus.essentials.harvest:
Right-click harvest
Right-click a fully grown crop to harvest it: wheat, carrots, potatoes, beetroot, nether wart, cocoa. It is replanted from its own seeds.

Hold V (vein mining) to harvest the whole connected field at once. Sneak to use an item on the crop instead.
guide.storagenexus.essentials.tnt:
Endermen and TNT
TNT, beds, respawn anchors, withers and end crystals work as in vanilla.

Endermen never pick up blocks. One that was already carrying a block before the mod was added can still put it down.
guide.storagenexus.essentials.slots:
Extra slots
Four slots that use no inventory space.

Above the offhand slot: the trinket slot (the Magnet) and the wings slot (an elytra, or any modded item that glides like one).

Under the crafting grid: the arrow slot and the totem slot.
guide.storagenexus.essentials.slots2:
Using the slots
Shift-click a Magnet, elytra, arrows or totem to send it to its slot, or right-click a Magnet or elytra in your hand to put it on.

In the creative inventory they sit right of the armor.
guide.storagenexus.essentials.slots3:
Slots and death
The slots are saved with you. On death they drop like the rest of your inventory (Curse of Vanishing destroys), unless keepInventory is on.
guide.storagenexus.essentials.arrows:
Arrow slot
Holds up to 64 arrows of any kind.

Bows and crossbows shoot from it after anything held in a hand and before arrows in your inventory.

Picked-up arrows fill it first.
guide.storagenexus.essentials.totem:
Totem slot
Takes a Totem of Undying, or any item with death protection.

If you would die with no totem in either hand, this one saves you, with the same effects as a held one. A held totem is used first.
guide.storagenexus.essentials.wings:
Wings slot
An elytra here glides exactly like one in the chest slot, so you can wear a chestplate too.

It wears down the same way; Unbreaking and Mending work, and its protection enchantments add to your armor's (80% cap still applies). Other players see it.
guide.storagenexus.essentials.magnet:
Magnet
Works while it is in your trinket slot. It pulls every item and experience orb in range, even through walls, using the normal pickup: full inventories, pickup delays and item owners still apply.
guide.storagenexus.essentials.magnet2:
Using the Magnet
Sneak + right-click: range 4, 8, 12 or 16 blocks.

M: on or off. It glints while on.

It pulls back what you drop after the 2-second pickup delay, so switch it off before throwing things away.
guide.storagenexus.essentials.elytra:
Elytra enchanting
At an anvil, elytra take Protection, Fire Protection, Blast Protection and Projectile Protection from enchanted books, and can hold all four at once, like any other armor piece now.
guide.storagenexus.essentials.enchants:
Higher levels
Protection (all four kinds), Unbreaking, Looting, Fortune and Respiration go up to level V: in the enchanting table, at an anvil (two IVs make a V), in loot chests and from villagers.

The anvil is never Too Expensive: any job can be done for its full cost in levels.
guide.storagenexus.essentials.enchants2:
Fewer limits
Mending works with Infinity, every protection goes on one piece, and Sharpness works with Smite.

Bane of Arthropods still excludes both, and Fortune still excludes Silk Touch.
guide.storagenexus.essentials.piglins:
Piglins
Any piece of netherite armor counts as gold armor: piglins stay neutral. Bartering still uses gold ingots.
guide.storagenexus.essentials.elevator:
Elevator
A flat Nexium platform. Put elevators at different heights in the same column (same X and Z), anywhere from the bottom of the world to the top.

Right-click one for the list of floors and click one to go there.
guide.storagenexus.essentials.elevator2:
Floors
Name the floor in the box and press Name; an empty name goes back to Floor 1, 2, 3 from the bottom. A floor with no room to stand (the two blocks above it are blocked) is greyed out.

Breaking an elevator forgets its name.
guide.storagenexus.essentials.librarian:
Master Librarian
At a Farm Assembler: pick Master Librarian, put in 12 villagers (spawn eggs or Captured Mobs) and press Build. He comes out as a Captured Mob: right-click a block to let him out.
guide.storagenexus.essentials.librarian2:
His trades
A book of every enchantment at its highest level, Mending and the other treasure ones too, but no curses. Prices are the villagers' own: 2 to 64 emeralds, plus a book each.

A librarian made this way can't be used as one of the 12.
guide.storagenexus.essentials.debris:
Ancient debris
Drops netherite scrap: 2 per block, multiplied by Fortune like diamond ore (Fortune I, II and III average 2.67, 3.5 and 4.4, up to 8). Silk Touch drops the block.
guide.storagenexus.mobs.mobs:
Picking up mobs
Sneak + right-click a mob with an empty hand to pick it up. You get a Captured Mob item that looks like its spawn egg, with a glint.

Right-click a block with it to let the mob out.
guide.storagenexus.mobs.kept:
What it keeps
A Captured Mob keeps everything about the mob: health, name, equipment, saddle and chests, villager profession and trades, horse stats, owner and age.
guide.storagenexus.mobs.limits:
Mob limits
The Ender Dragon and the Wither can't be picked up. Only a pet's owner can pick it up.

Not in Adventure mode, nor inside spawn protection (unless you are an operator).
guide.storagenexus.mobs.know:
Good to know
Sneak + right-click a tamed horse, donkey or llama with an item still opens its inventory.

A picked-up villager gives up its bed and workstation; it finds new ones when let out.

Riders get off and a lead drops.
guide.storagenexus.mobs.know2:
The item
Monsters can't be let out on Peaceful (the item stays in your hand).

A Captured Mob item never despawns and survives fire, lava, explosions and cactus.
guide.storagenexus.mobs.elixir:
Bedrock Breaking
Drink the Elixir for 5 minutes of Bedrock Breaker: a diamond or netherite pickaxe (or AIOT) then mines bedrock like obsidian.

Bedrock drops nothing, and any bedrock breaks, even the bottom layer above the void. Careful!
guide.storagenexus.mobs.assembler:
Farm Assembler
Makes the one-block farms and the Master Librarian. Right-click it, pick one from the list on the left and put in what it needs.

The right side shows how much of each material is in, with a bar, and a tick when a line is done.
guide.storagenexus.mobs.assembler2:
Filling it
Add from inventory moves everything it still needs out of your inventory. Shift-clicking items, or hoppers above or beside it, add them too.

It only takes what is still needed, and picking something else gives back what was in. When all is in, press Build and take the result from the slot.
guide.storagenexus.mobs.farm:
Iron Farm
A one-block iron farm. Place it anywhere.

Every 7.5 seconds it makes a golem's drops: 3-5 iron and 0-2 poppies, about 1,900 iron an hour.
guide.storagenexus.mobs.farm2:
Using the farm
Right-click it to see the output, a bar to the next golem and the bread slot.

Hoppers and pipes take the output from below, and only from below. Nothing can be put in by hopper.
guide.storagenexus.mobs.make:
Making one
At a Farm Assembler: pick Iron Farm in its list, put in the materials below and press Build. The Iron Farm appears in the slot next to the button.
guide.storagenexus.mobs.recipe:
Iron Farm recipe
Zombies: 4
Villagers: 12
Torches: 33
Slabs: 20
Signs: 16
Trapdoors: 12
Beds: 12
Smooth Stone: 1,408
guide.storagenexus.mobs.notes:
Recipe notes
Zombies and villagers can be spawn eggs or Captured Mobs (zombie, husk, drowned or zombie villager all count).

Torches, slabs, signs, trapdoors and beds can be any kind.
guide.storagenexus.mobs.notes2:
Recipe notes, more
Amounts are totals: any mix of kinds counts, in any order. The Assembler only takes what is still needed and its screen shows what is missing.
guide.storagenexus.mobs.bread:
Bread
Put bread in the bread slot and the farm works 10x faster (about 19,000 iron an hour), eating a loaf every 30 seconds.

When the last loaf is eaten, the slot locks for 10x as long as the boost lasted.
guide.storagenexus.mobs.bread2:
Bread cooldown
A full stack of 64 loaves is 32 minutes of boost, then 5 h 20 min of cooldown. The farm keeps working at normal speed meanwhile.

Hover the empty bread slot to see how long is left.
guide.storagenexus.mobs.running:
Running the farm
When the output is full, or a redstone signal reaches it, the farm waits and doesn't eat bread (a bread cooldown keeps counting down). The screen says which.

Breaking it drops the Iron Farm with its boost and cooldown kept.
guide.storagenexus.mobs.farms:
More farms
Five more one-block farms, made at the Farm Assembler like the Iron Farm. Mobs can be spawn eggs or Captured Mobs.

Hoppers below take the output; redstone pauses it.
guide.storagenexus.mobs.breeder:
Villager Breeder
2 villagers, 4 beds, 2 composters, 8 hay bales, 2 emerald blocks, 2,880 planks.

A baby villager (Captured Mob) every 20 minutes, for 3 bread or 12 carrots, potatoes or beetroot.
guide.storagenexus.mobs.barter:
Piglin Barter Farm
2 piglins, 9 gold blocks, 16 soul sand, 16 planks, 3,136 netherrack.

1 gold ingot every 6 seconds for the real piglin barter loot. Hoppers feed it from the top or sides.
guide.storagenexus.mobs.zpiglin:
Zombified Piglin Farm
4 zombified piglins, 8 magma blocks, 20 nether bricks, 16 gold ingots, 3,008 netherrack.

Every 4 seconds: gold nuggets (about 3) and a 7.5% gold ingot, as with Looting V.
guide.storagenexus.mobs.witherfarm:
Wither Skeleton Farm
4 wither skeletons, 16 nether brick fences, 8 soul sand, 4 coal blocks, 4 magma blocks, 2,944 netherrack.

Every 6 seconds: coal, bones and a 7.5% skull.
guide.storagenexus.mobs.shulkerfarm:
Shulker Farm
4 shulkers, 32 purpur blocks, 8 end rods, 8 ender pearls, 3,008 end stone bricks.

Every 30 seconds: a shulker shell about 4 times in 5.
guide.storagenexus.essentials.freezer:
Freezer
Fill it with water, by bucket or pipe, and it freezes ice: 1 bucket, 5 seconds each.

Its button picks ice, packed ice (9 buckets, 45 s) or blue ice (81 buckets, 90 s). Water is used up steadily.

Hoppers below take the ice.
guide.storagenexus.essentials.freezer2:
Dyeing
Dye a Freezer in the crafting grid like leather armor; dyes mix. Body and frame take the colour; frost, glow and water don't.

A cauldron of water washes it.

Packed ice crafts into 9 ice, blue ice into 9 packed ice.
guide.storagenexus.essentials.sand:
Soul sand to sand
A blast furnace smelts soul sand into sand, with no experience, at the speed of an ore.

The Piglin Barter Farm gives soul sand, so this turns a barter overflow into sand.
